1: //! # pathland-render-gtk
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **GTK4 renderer**. It consumes opcode frames (via
4: //! [`crate::host::RenderTree`]) and maps them **incrementally** onto native GTK4
5: //! widgets — `GtkBox` for stacks, `GtkLabel` for text, `GtkButton` for buttons.
6: //!
7: //! This is the only place in the desktop path that touches GTK/glib/pango APIs.
8: //! Demos author their UI with the Pathland DSL and drive this renderer; they
9: //! never call GTK directly.
10: //!
11: //! ## Rust host
12: //!
13: //! `GtkRenderer::run(app_id, title, ring, on_event)` owns the `gtk::Application`
14: //! / `ApplicationWindow` / main loop, pumps the shared ring (frames in, events
15: //! out), and dispatches raw-input [`Event`]s back to the application.
16: //!
17: //! ## Java host
18: //!
19: //! The `pathland_gtk_*` C ABI (`capi` module) exposes the same renderer to a
20: //! foreign host (Java via JNA): `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)` runs GTK
21: //! in-process over the `pathland-view-native` host's shared ring.
22:

49: /// The bidirectional transport surface the renderer pumps: frames in
50: /// (guest → host) and events out (host → guest).
51: ///
52: /// The renderer **never drains events** — it only writes them as `EVENT`
53: /// opcodes. The host (application) drains the event ring itself, so raw inputs
54: /// return to the app through the opcode engine, symmetric with how frames flow
55: /// to the renderer.
56: pub trait Pump {
57:     /// Read the next guest → host frame.
58:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
59:     /// Write a host → guest raw input as an `EVENT` opcode.
60:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
61: }
62: 
63: impl Pump for RingTransport {
64:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
65:         FrameSource::next_frame(self)
66:     }
67:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
68:         DriverTransport::send_input(self, event)
69:     }
70: }
71: 
72: /// The GTK4 renderer: a retained `id → gtk::Widget` map kept in sync with the
73: /// opcode stream, applying deltas incrementally.
74: pub struct GtkRenderer {
75:     tree: RenderTree,
76:     widgets: HashMap<u32, gtk::Widget>,
77:     /// node id → listener bitmask already attached (idempotency guard so delta
78:     /// frames don't double-attach controllers).
79:     attached_listeners: HashMap<u32, u32>,
80:     /// node id → composite-body box (Composite Override Mode): the container
81:     /// that holds a control's custom child tree.
82:     composite_boxes: HashMap<u32, gtk::Widget>,
83:     /// Set once before the first render so buttons can report clicks.
84:     event_sink: Option<Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut(Event)>>>,
85:     /// A widget's style context captured at first build, used to enrich the
86:     /// design-token defaults with GTK-native theme colors (`None` headless).
87:     native_ctx: Option<gtk::StyleContext>,
88:     /// `AdwNavigationView` handles for navigation slots (a container carrying
89:     /// the `ROUTE` property), keyed by slot node id.
90:     nav_views: HashMap<u32, NavigationView>,
91:     /// Per-navigation-slot page stack mirror (shared with the `popped`
92:     /// handler), keyed by slot node id. The native `AdwNavigationView` is the
93:     /// renderer's rendered-output cache of the app's back-stack; this vec is
94:     /// the adapter's depth bookkeeping (the widget's own page stack is not
95:     /// directly countable).
96:     nav_pages: HashMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<Vec<libadwaita::NavigationPage>>>>,
97:     /// Per-navigation-slot "reconciling" flag: while the renderer pops pages
98:     /// itself (a route change it already applied), the `popped` signal must not
99:     /// be re-emitted as a back request — the app already knows it navigated.
100:     nav_reconciling: HashMap<u32, Rc<Cell<bool>>>,
101:     /// Per-node native media streams (AUDIO/VIDEO nodes), the rendered output
102:     /// for app-driven playback. Playback is driven by the node's media control
103:     /// properties; media events report back through the event sink.
104:     media_players: HashMap<u32, MediaPlayer>,
105:     /// Per-node cache of the last applied fixed-size image content, so steady-
106:     /// state frames don't re-decode: (source, box width, box height, content mode).
107:     image_cache: HashMap<u32, (String, i32, i32, u32)>,
108: }
109: 
110: impl Default for GtkRenderer {
111:     fn default() -> Self {
112:         Self::new()
113:     }
114: }

116: impl GtkRenderer {
117:     /// Create an empty renderer. Call [`GtkRenderer::apply_frame`] per frame.
118:     pub fn new() -> Self {
119:         Self {
120:             tree: RenderTree::default(),
121:             widgets: HashMap::new(),
122:             attached_listeners: HashMap::new(),
123:             composite_boxes: HashMap::new(),
124:             event_sink: None,
125:             native_ctx: None,
126:             nav_views: HashMap::new(),
127:             nav_pages: HashMap::new(),
128:             nav_reconciling: HashMap::new(),
129:             media_players: HashMap::new(),
130:             image_cache: HashMap::new(),
131:         }
132:     }
133: 
134:     /// Set the event sink (called when a native widget reports an input).
135:     pub fn set_event_sink(&mut self, sink: Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut(Event)>>) {
136:         self.event_sink = Some(sink);
137:     }
138: 
139:     /// The effective color scheme the renderer resolved from the platform.
140:     pub fn scheme(&self) -> Scheme {
141:         self.tree.scheme()
142:     }
143: 
144:     /// Set the effective color scheme (renderer-derived, never carried by the
145:     /// protocol) and re-resolve every design token — native defaults for the
146:     /// new scheme are re-enriched from the GTK theme when a widget exists, then
147:     /// all token-referencing properties re-resolve and the widget tree re-applies.
148:     pub fn set_scheme(&mut self, scheme: Scheme) {
149:         self.enrich_native_defaults();
150:         self.tree.set_scheme(scheme);
151:         self.sync();
152:     }
153: 
154:     /// One-time best-effort: replace Tier-1 default tokens the current GTK
155:     /// theme can resolve (`@theme_*` named colors) with native colors, using
156:     /// the first widget's style context. Headless → concrete fallbacks remain.
157:     fn enrich_native_defaults(&mut self) {
158:         if let Some(ctx) = self.native_ctx.as_ref() {
159:             let scheme = self.tree.scheme();
160:             let (base, dark) = tokens::enrich_defaults(
161:                 &|name| tokens::lookup_color(ctx, name),
162:                 scheme,
163:             );
164:             self.tree.set_defaults(base, dark);
165:         }
166:     }
167: 
168:     /// Apply one frame of opcode deltas and reconcile the GTK widget tree.
169:     ///
170:     /// Unchanged widgets are preserved (no full rebuild); only nodes the frame
171:     /// touched get their native widget created, updated, or removed.
172:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
173:         self.tree.apply_frame(frame);
174:         self.sync();
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// The root widget (the native element for the tree root).
178:     pub fn root_widget(&self) -> Option<gtk::Widget> {
179:         self.tree
180:             .root()
181:             .and_then(|n| self.widgets.get(&n.id).cloned())
182:     }
183: 
184:     /// Reconcile the GTK widget tree against the current `RenderTree`.
185:     fn sync(&mut self) {
186:         // 1. Drop widgets for nodes that no longer exist.
187:         let live: std::collections::HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
188:         let stale: Vec<u32> = self
189:             .widgets
190:             .keys()
191:             .copied()
192:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
193:             .collect();
194:         for id in stale {
195:             self.widgets.remove(&id);
196:             self.attached_listeners.remove(&id);
197:             self.composite_boxes.remove(&id);
198:             self.nav_views.remove(&id);
199:             self.nav_pages.remove(&id);
200:             self.nav_reconciling.remove(&id);
201:             if let Some(player) = self.media_players.remove(&id) {
202:                 player.teardown();
203:             }
204:             self.image_cache.remove(&id);
205:         }
206: 
207:         // 2. Pre-order walk: get-or-create widgets, update text/style, and
208:         //    reconcile each stack's child list/order.
209:         if let Some(root_id) = self.tree.root().map(|n| n.id) {
210:             self.sync_node(root_id);
211:         }
212:     }
213: 
214:     fn sync_node(&mut self, id: u32) {
215:         let Some(node) = self.tree.node(id).cloned() else {
216:             return;
217:         };
218: 
219:         let widget = self.get_or_create(id, &node);
220:         // The first get_or_create may have just enriched the token defaults
221:         // with GTK theme colors; re-read the node so the values applied now
222:         // are the native-resolved ones, not the pre-enrichment fallbacks.
223:         let node = self.tree.node(id).cloned().unwrap_or(node);
224:         self.update(widget, &node);
225: 
226:         // Recurse into children (build them first so they exist to attach).
227:         let children = node.children.clone();
228:         for child in &children {
229:             self.sync_node(*child);
230:         }
231: 
232:         // Containers: reconcile the native children (order/content/positions)
233:         // against the tree.
234:         if is_container(node.component_type) {
235:             self.sync_container(id, &children, &node);
236:         } else if is_composite(&node) {
237:             self.sync_composite_children(id, &children);
238:         }
239:     }
240: 
241:     /// Composite Override Mode: attach a control's custom child tree as a box
242:     /// wrapped by the control's native shell (the widget itself).
243:     ///
244:     /// Composite bodies attach to button-like controls (`GtkButton` and
245:     /// subclasses — `ToggleButton`, `CheckButton`, `MenuButton`); other controls
246:     /// ignore children.
247:     ///
248:     /// The body box's orientation follows the HTML renderer's composite layout:
249:     /// a `BUTTON` body is a **horizontal row** (`.pathland-button` is
250:     /// `display:inline-flex; align-items:center`), while `TOGGLE`/`MENU` bodies
251:     /// stay **vertical** (HTML wraps those as block/inline-block).
252:     fn sync_composite_children(&mut self, parent_id: u32, children: &[u32]) {
253:         let Some(parent) = self.widgets.get(&parent_id).cloned() else {
254:             return;
255:         };
256:         let Ok(btn) = parent.clone().downcast::<gtk::Button>() else {
257:             return;
258:         };
259:         let horizontal = self
260:             .tree
261:             .node(parent_id)
262:             .is_some_and(|n| composite_horizontal(n.component_type));
263:         // The body's SPACING comes from the control node itself: a composite
264:         // control whose label flattened a stack (e.g. `Button.of(HStack, …)`)
265:         // carries that stack's `SPACING` on the button node, and the button's
266:         // body box must reproduce the gap (HTML emits `gap` on the `<button>`).
267:         // Re-applied on every reconcile so a `SPACING` delta takes effect.
268:         let spacing = self
269:             .tree
270:             .node(parent_id)
271:             .map(layout::spacing)
272:             .unwrap_or(0);
273:         // The button's own main/cross-axis alignment is governed by its parent
274:         // stack's per-child rule in `sync_stack_children` (LAYOUT.md: a
275:         // composite control hugs on the main axis unless it is `FILL`-sized).
276:         let box_widget: gtk::Widget = if let Some(bx) = self.composite_boxes.get(&parent_id).cloned() {
277:             bx
278:         } else {
279:             let bx = GtkBox::new(
280:                 if horizontal {
281:                     gtk::Orientation::Horizontal
282:                 } else {
283:                     gtk::Orientation::Vertical
284:                 },
285:                 spacing,
286:             );
287:             btn.set_child(Some(&bx));
288:             let bxw: gtk::Widget = bx.upcast();
289:             self.composite_boxes.insert(parent_id, bxw.clone());
290:             bxw
291:         };
292:         if let Ok(bx) = box_widget.clone().downcast::<GtkBox>() {
293:             bx.set_spacing(spacing);
294:         }
295:         // A horizontal (BUTTON) body centers its children on the cross axis,
296:         // matching the HTML button's `align-items:center`.
297:         if horizontal {
298:             for child_id in children {
299:                 if let Some(w) = self.widgets.get(child_id) {
300:                     w.set_valign(Align::Center);
301:                 }
302:             }
303:         }
304:         self.reconcile_box_children(&box_widget, children);
305:     }

308:         if let Some(w) = self.widgets.get(&id) {
309:             return w.clone();
310:         }

527:     /// Drive a node's native media stream from its control properties (the
528:     /// app-driven media contract, spec/EVENTS.md Media): source, playback
529:     /// state, position (seek, echo-guarded), and volume.
530:     fn sync_media(&mut self, id: u32, node: &HostNode) {
531:         let source = node
532:             .string_property(property_id::AUDIO_SOURCE)
533:             .or_else(|| node.string_property(property_id::VIDEO_SOURCE));
534:         let Some(source) = source else {
535:             // A media node with no source: nothing to play; drop any stream.
536:             if let Some(player) = self.media_players.remove(&id) {
537:                 player.teardown();
538:             }
539:             return;
540:         };
541:         let resolved = resolve_asset(source);
542:         let player = match self.media_players.get_mut(&id) {
543:             Some(player) if player.source == resolved => player,
544:             _ => {
545:                 if let Some(old) = self.media_players.remove(&id) {
546:                     old.teardown();
547:                 }
548:                 let Some(player) = self.create_media_player(id, resolved.clone()) else {
549:                     // GStreamer unavailable: nothing to play for this node.
550:                     return;
551:                 };
552:                 self.media_players.insert(id, player);
553:                 self.media_players.get_mut(&id).expect("just inserted")
554:             }
555:         };
556: 
557:         // Playback state: the node's current value (a source change re-emits only
558:         // AUDIO_SOURCE, so the retained PLAYBACK_STATE is authoritative — a skip
559:         // while playing therefore resumes automatically).
560:         let playing = node.u32_property(property_id::PLAYBACK_STATE, 0) != 0;
561:         player.requested_playing.set(playing);
562:         let state = if playing {
563:             gst::State::Playing
564:         } else {
565:             gst::State::Paused
566:         };
567:         let _ = player.pipeline.set_state(state);
568: 
569:         // Seek — only when meaningful: the app echoes every MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED
570:         // back as MEDIA_POSITION, so a near-identical write must NOT seek (it
571:         // would interrupt just-started playback and echo the position around).
572:         let target = f64::from(node.f32_property(property_id::MEDIA_POSITION, 0.0));
573:         let now = player
574:             .playbin
575:             .query_position::<gst::ClockTime>()
576:             .map(|t| t.nseconds() as f64 / 1_000_000_000.0)
577:             .unwrap_or(0.0);
578:         if should_seek(now, target) {
579:             let _ = player.playbin.seek_simple(
580:                 gst::SeekFlags::FLUSH,
581:                 gst::ClockTime::from_seconds_f64(target),
582:             );
583:             player.suppress_until.set(monotonic_ms() + 250);
584:         }
585: 
586:         let volume = node.f32_property(property_id::MEDIA_VOLUME, 1.0);
587:         player.playbin.set_property("volume", f64::from(volume.clamp(0.0, 1.0)));
588:     }

590:     /// Create a media player for a node: a GStreamer `playbin` pipeline driven by
591: /// the node's control properties, with a periodic reporter that both polls the
592: /// stream position (`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`) and drains the pipeline bus for
593: /// `EOS` (`MEDIA_ENDED`) / errors (play-state false). The bus is polled on the
594: /// main thread (not via `connect_message`, which requires a `Send` closure the
595: /// renderer's `Rc`-based sink cannot provide). Returns `None` when GStreamer
596: /// is unavailable.
597: fn create_media_player(&mut self, id: u32, resolved: String) -> Option<MediaPlayer> {
598:     let (pipeline, playbin) = build_playbin(&resolved)?;
599:     let suppress_until = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u64));
600:     let last_reported = Rc::new(Cell::new(0f32));
601:     let requested_playing = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
602:     let Some(sink) = self.event_sink.clone() else {
603:         return Some(MediaPlayer {
604:             pipeline,
605:             playbin,
606:             source: resolved,
607:             requested_playing,
608:             suppress_until,
609:             timer: None,
610:         });
611:     };
612: 
613:     // Periodic position reporter (~4 Hz while playing, mirroring the web
614:     // client's `timeupdate` cadence). Suppressed briefly after a seek. Also
615:     // drains the pipeline bus: EOS → MEDIA_ENDED, an error → play-state false
616:     // (so the app's play button isn't left stuck on a failed stream).
617:     let timer_pipeline = pipeline.clone();
618:     let timer_playbin = playbin.clone();
619:     let timer_sink = sink;
620:     let timer_suppress = suppress_until.clone();
621:     let timer_last = last_reported.clone();
622:     let timer_playing = requested_playing.clone();
623:     let timer = glib::timeout_add_local(Duration::from_millis(250), move || {
624:         if let Some(bus) = timer_pipeline.bus() {
625:             while let Some(msg) = bus.pop() {
626:                 match msg.view() {
627:                     gst::MessageView::Eos(_) => {
628:                         timer_sink.borrow_mut()(Event::MediaEnded { target: id });
629:                         timer_playing.set(false);
630:                     }
631:                     gst::MessageView::Error(err) => {
632:                         eprintln!(
633:                             "pathland-gtk media error: {}",
634:                             err.error().message()
635:                         );
636:                         timer_playing.set(false);
637:                         timer_sink.borrow_mut()(Event::MediaPlayStateChanged {
638:                             target: id,
639:                             playing: false,
640:                         });
641:                     }
642:                     _ => {}
643:                 }
644:             }
645:         }
646:         if timer_playing.get() && monotonic_ms() >= timer_suppress.get() {
647:             let seconds = timer_playbin
648:                 .query_position::<gst::ClockTime>()
649:                 .map(|t| t.nseconds() as f32 / 1_000_000_000.0)
650:                 .unwrap_or(0.0);
651:             if should_report_time(timer_last.get(), seconds) {
652:                 timer_last.set(seconds);
653:                 timer_sink.borrow_mut()(Event::MediaTimeUpdated {
654:                     target: id,
655:                     seconds,
656:                 });
657:             }
658:         }
659:         glib::ControlFlow::Continue
660:     });
661:     Some(MediaPlayer {
662:         pipeline,
663:         playbin,
664:         source: resolved,
665:         requested_playing,
666:         suppress_until,
667:         timer: Some(timer),
668:     })
669: }

671:     /// Apply an image node: a fixed `WIDTH`×`HEIGHT` (logical points) scales the
672:     /// decoded content into that box (Fit = contain/letterbox, Fill = cover/crop,
673:     /// mirroring the web's `object-fit` and SwiftUI content modes); otherwise the
674:     /// file is loaded natively and the picture scales itself. The scaled box is
675:     /// cached per node so steady-state frames don't re-decode.
676:     fn apply_image(&mut self, node: &HostNode, pic: &gtk::Picture, src: &str) {

681:             .max(0.0) as u32;

683:             fixed_size(node, property_id::WIDTH),
684:             fixed_size(node, property_id::HEIGHT),
685:         ) else {
686:             // No fixed points box: load natively and let the picture fit itself.
687:             pic.set_filename(Some(&resolved));

690:         };
691:         if self.image_cache.get(&node.id) == Some(&(resolved.clone(), box_w, box_h, mode)) {

752:     /// Reconcile a stack's children: apply the LAYOUT.md per-child alignment
753:     /// rule (main axis: only `FILL`/greedy children stretch, leftover goes to
754:     /// them; cross axis: only `FILL`/greedy children stretch, everything else
755:     /// keeps its size and is positioned by the stack's `ALIGNMENT`, default
756:     /// Leading) and re-append the tree-ordered child widgets.
757:     ///
758:     /// The `hexpand`/`vexpand` flags are set from the SAME effective-FILL
759:     /// decision, so a non-FILL main-axis child is explicitly non-expanding
760:     /// (`valign=Start`, `vexpand=false`) and can never claim leftover space —
761:     /// a `GtkBox` otherwise hands it to children left at GTK's default
762:     /// `Align::Fill`/expand state, which spreads e.g. a library's rows.
763:     fn sync_stack_children(&mut self, parent_id: u32, children: &[u32], node: &HostNode) {
764:         let Some(parent) = self.widgets.get(&parent_id).cloned() else {
765:             return;
766:         };
767:         let Some(_bx) = parent.downcast_ref::<GtkBox>() else {
768:             return;
769:         };
770:         let Some(l) = layout::stack_layout(node) else {
771:             return;
772:         };
773:         let stack_align = layout::stack_align_option(node);
774:         // Fill propagation: a Hug child stack that contains a FILL child fills
775:         // the axis (resolved through the tree).
776:         for child_id in children {
777:             let Some(w) = self.widgets.get(child_id).cloned() else {
778:                 continue;
779:             };
780:             let Some(cn) = self.tree.node(*child_id) else {
781:                 continue;
782:             };
783:             let main = layout::main_axis_align(cn, l.orientation, &self.tree);
784:             let cross = layout::cross_axis_align(cn, l.orientation, stack_align, &self.tree);
785:             if layout::cross_axis_is_horizontal(l.orientation) {
786:                 w.set_halign(cross);
787:                 w.set_valign(main);
788:                 w.set_hexpand(cross == Align::Fill);
789:                 w.set_vexpand(main == Align::Fill);
790:             } else {
791:                 w.set_halign(main);
792:                 w.set_valign(cross);
793:                 w.set_hexpand(main == Align::Fill);
794:                 w.set_vexpand(cross == Align::Fill);
795:             }
796:         }
797:         self.reconcile_box_children(&parent, children);
798:     }

800:     /// Reconcile a `GtkGrid`'s children at their flattened cell positions (spec
801:     /// §GridRow): a `GRID_ROW`'s children are one row's cells; bare cells
802:     /// auto-flow row-major (column-major for a horizontal `LAZY_HGRID`).
803:     fn sync_grid_children(&mut self, parent_id: u32, _children: &[u32], node: &HostNode) {
804:         let Some(parent) = self.widgets.get(&parent_id).cloned() else {
805:             return;
806:         };
807:         let Some(grid) = parent.downcast_ref::<gtk::Grid>() else {
808:             return;
809:         };
810:         let cells = layout::grid_cells(node, &self.tree);
811:         // SPACING → uniform row + column gap (HTML renders `gap` on grids).
812:         let gap = layout::spacing(node);
813:         grid.set_row_spacing(gap as u32);
814:         grid.set_column_spacing(gap as u32);
815:         // Per-cell alignment (LAYOUT.md): a `FILL`/greedy cell stretches on an
816:         // axis, anything else keeps its size and is positioned at the start.
817:         let grid_align = node.properties.get(&property_id::ALIGNMENT).copied().unwrap_or(0);
818:         for (cell, _, _) in &cells {
819:             if let (Some(w), Some(cn)) = (self.widgets.get(cell), self.tree.node(*cell)) {
820:                 w.set_halign(layout::grid_cell_align(cn, layout::Axis::Horizontal, grid_align));
821:                 w.set_valign(layout::grid_cell_align(cn, layout::Axis::Vertical, grid_align));
822:             }
823:         }
824:         if grid_matches(grid, &cells, &self.widgets) {
825:             return;
826:         }
827:         // Rebuild: remove all current children, then attach at target cells.
828:         for w in child_widgets(&parent) {
829:             grid.remove(&w);
830:         }
831:         for (cell, row, col) in &cells {
832:             if let Some(w) = self.widgets.get(cell) {
833:                 grid.attach(w, *col as i32, *row as i32, 1, 1);
834:             }
835:         }
836:     }

858:     /// Reconcile a `GtkOverlay`: every child is an overlay (later = drawn on top),
859:     /// keeps its own size unless it is effectively `FILL`, and is positioned by
860:     /// the ZStack's `ALIGNMENT` on **both** axes (default Leading/Start) —
861:     /// spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack.
862:     fn sync_overlay_children(&mut self, parent_id: u32, children: &[u32], node: &HostNode) {
863:         let Some(parent) = self.widgets.get(&parent_id).cloned() else {
864:             return;
865:         };
866:         let Some(ov) = parent.downcast_ref::<gtk::Overlay>() else {
867:             return;
868:         };
869:         let raw_align = node.properties.get(&property_id::ALIGNMENT).copied().unwrap_or(0);
870:         let target: Vec<gtk::Widget> = children
871:             .iter()
872:             .filter_map(|id| self.widgets.get(id).cloned())
873:             .collect();
874:         // Apply per-child alignment on every reconcile (cheap; needed even when
875:         // the child set is unchanged, e.g. an ALIGNMENT delta).
876:         let position = |child_id: &u32, w: &gtk::Widget| {
877:             let Some(cn) = self.tree.node(*child_id) else {
878:                 return;
879:             };
880:             let halign = if layout::effective_fill(cn, layout::Axis::Horizontal, false, &self.tree) {
881:                 Align::Fill
882:             } else {
883:                 layout::align_h(raw_align)
884:             };
885:             let valign = if layout::effective_fill(cn, layout::Axis::Vertical, false, &self.tree) {
886:                 Align::Fill
887:             } else {
888:                 layout::align_v(raw_align)
889:             };
890:             w.set_halign(halign);
891:             w.set_valign(valign);
892:         };
893:         if child_widgets(&parent) == target {
894:             for (child_id, w) in children.iter().zip(&target) {
895:                 position(child_id, w);
896:             }
897:             return;
898:         }
899:         for w in child_widgets(&parent) {
900:             ov.remove_overlay(&w);
901:         }
902:         for (child_id, w) in children.iter().zip(&target) {
903:             position(child_id, w);
904:             ov.add_overlay(w);
905:         }
906:     }

928:     /// Reconcile a navigation slot's pages against the app's current destination.
929:     /// The slot carries exactly one child — the current destination subtree —
930:     /// plus a `ROUTE` string and a `NAV_DEPTH` (U32) back-stack depth. The
931:     /// adapter reconciles the `AdwNavigationView` page stack **by depth**:
932:     ///
933:     /// - **deeper than the current stack** → `push` a new page for the route,
934:     /// - **shallower** → `pop` pages down to the target depth (back, or a
935:     ///   deep-link stack reset),
936:     /// - **same depth, new route** → **replace** the top page (a guard
937:     ///   redirect / `replace()`),
938:     /// - **same depth, same route** → refresh the top page's content in place
939:     ///   (a signal-driven update of the current destination).
940:     ///
941:     /// The back-stack stays app-owned; the `AdwNavigationView` is only the
942:     /// renderer's rendered-output cache of it. Programmatic pops here are
943:     /// guarded so they never re-emit as a back request.
944:     fn sync_navigation_children(&mut self, slot_id: u32, children: &[u32], node: &HostNode) {
945:         let Some(nav) = self.nav_views.get(&slot_id).cloned() else {
946:             return;
947:         };
948:         let Some(target) = children
949:             .first()
950:             .and_then(|id| self.widgets.get(id).cloned())
951:         else {
952:             return;
953:         };
954:         // Without a ROUTE the slot is not a navigation slot (the renderer would
955:         // not have promoted it). Depth defaults to 1.
956:         let route = node.string_property(property_id::ROUTE).unwrap_or_default();
957:         let depth = node.u32_property(property_id::NAV_DEPTH, 1).max(1) as usize;
958:         // Custom chrome mode: the developer owns all nav UI → no native chrome.
959:         let custom_chrome = is_custom_chrome(node);
960: 
961:         let stack = self.nav_pages.entry(slot_id).or_default().clone();
962:         self.attach_nav_back(slot_id, &nav, &stack);
963: 
964:         let mut pages = stack.borrow_mut();
965: 
966:         // Pop down to the app's depth (an app-driven pop or a stack reset). The

2: //!
3: //! A foreign host (Java via JNA) drives the `pathland-view-native` flat world to
4: //! build/emit the retained tree, then calls `pathland_gtk_run` to hand the
5: //! renderer its shared ring and run GTK in-process. Raw-input events are
6: //! reported back through a C callback (`void (*)(u32 targetId)`).
7: //!
8: //! A second route — `pathland_gtk_run_ring` — lets a host that emits opcodes
9: //! itself (e.g. the Java DSL's `libpathland_core` ring) hand the renderer the
10: //! borrowed ring directly, with no `pathland-view-native` host involved.

22: /// A host-supplied event callback, invoked (with no payload) when the renderer
23: /// has written a raw input into the host → guest event ring. The host drains the
24: /// ring itself (via `pathland_native_drain_events`) to receive the events.
25: pub type EventCallback = extern "C" fn();

28: /// resolve against (see [`crate::resolve_asset`]). Call before `pathland_gtk_run`
29: /// / `pathland_gtk_run_ring`. A null pointer clears the root.
30: #[no_mangle]

32:     if dir.is_null() {
33:         set_asset_root(String::new());
34:         return;
35:     }
36:     let Ok(bytes) = CStr::from_ptr(dir).to_str() else {
37:         return;
38:     };

42: /// A `Pump` over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost` owned by the foreign host.
43: ///
44: /// The renderer borrows the host through a raw pointer for the duration of
45: /// `pathland_gtk_run`; the foreign host keeps driving the same host (via its
46: /// own handle) from the event callback. All access is on the GTK main thread.
47: struct NativeHostHandle(*mut NativeHost);

49: impl Pump for NativeHostHandle {
50:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
51:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (GTK main thread); the foreign host must not
52:         // destroy the host until `pathland_gtk_run` returns.
53:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }

71:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }

1322: /// A `file://` URI for a local path (percent-encoding the characters that break
1323: /// a URI).
1324: fn file_uri(path: &str) -> String {
1325:     let mut uri = String::from("file://");
1326:     for ch in path.chars() {
1327:         match ch {
1328:             ' ' => uri.push_str("%20"),
1329:             '#' => uri.push_str("%23"),
1330:             '?' => uri.push_str("%3F"),
1331:             '%' => uri.push_str("%25"),
1332:             _ => uri.push(ch),
1333:         }
1334:     }
1335:     uri
1336: }

1349: /// Whether a grid's cells already sit at their target (row, col) positions.

1351:     grid: &gtk::Grid,
1352:     cells: &[(u32, u32, u32)],
1353:     widgets: &HashMap<u32, gtk::Widget>,
1354: ) -> bool {
1355:     if child_widgets(&grid.clone().upcast()).len() != cells.len() {
1356:         return false;

1499: /// with the fill color.

1501:     let kind = node.f32_property(property_id::SHAPE_KIND, 0.0).round() as u8;

1506:         let (w, h) = (w as f64, h as f64);

1508:         match kind {
1509:             0 | 4 => {
1510:                 cr.arc(w / 2.0, h / 2.0, w.min(h) / 2.0, 0.0, std::f64::consts::TAU);

1516:                 cr.rectangle(0.0, 0.0, w, h);
1517:                 let _ = cr.fill();
1518:             }

1520:                 let _ = radius;
1521:                 cr.rectangle(0.0, 0.0, w, h);

1523:             }
1524:             _ => {

1777: /// Where content of size `(src_w, src_h)` sits inside a `(box_w, box_h)` points
1778: /// box for a content mode: `Fit` (0) scales to fit, centered (letterboxed);
1779: /// `Fill` (1) scales to cover and crops. Returns the target `(x, y, w, h)` in
1780: /// box coordinates (for `Fit`, `w`/`h` are the fitted content size and `x`/`y`
1781: /// its centered offset; for `Fill`, the crop window over the scaled content).
1782: fn fit_rect(src_w: i32, src_h: i32, box_w: i32, box_h: i32, mode: u32) -> (i32, i32, i32, i32) {
1783:     let sw = src_w.max(1) as f64;
1784:     let sh = src_h.max(1) as f64;
1785:     let bw = box_w.max(1) as f64;
1786:     let bh = box_h.max(1) as f64;
1787:     let scale = if mode == 1 {
1788:         (bw / sw).max(bh / sh) // cover: fill the box
1789:     } else {
1790:         (bw / sw).min(bh / sh) // fit: fit within the box
1791:     };
1792:     let tw = (sw * scale).round() as i32;
1793:     let th = (sh * scale).round() as i32;
1794:     let x = (box_w - tw) / 2;
1795:     let y = (box_h - th) / 2;
1796:     (x, y, tw, th)
1797: }

1799: /// Decode a fixed-size image into a `box_w`×`box_h` points box: `Fit` (0)
1800: /// scales to fit and centers it on a transparent canvas (letterbox); `Fill` (1)
1801: /// scales to cover and crops to the box. The box-sized pixbuf makes
1802: /// `GtkPicture`'s natural size equal the requested box (logical points),
1803: /// matching the web/SwiftUI. Returns `None` on decode/scale failure.
1804: fn scale_image_to_box(path: &str, box_w: i32, box_h: i32, mode: u32) -> Option<gdk_pixbuf::Pixbuf> {
1805:     use gdk_pixbuf::{Colorspace, InterpType, Pixbuf};
1806:     let src = Pixbuf::from_file(path).ok()?;
1807:     if box_w <= 0 || box_h <= 0 {
1808:         return Some(src);
1809:     }
1810:     let (x, y, tw, th) = fit_rect(src.width(), src.height(), box_w, box_h, mode);
1811:     let scaled = src
1812:         .scale_simple(tw.max(1), th.max(1), InterpType::Bilinear)?;
1813:     if mode == 1 {
1814:         // Cover: crop the box-sized region from the center of the scaled content.
1815:         Some(scaled.new_subpixbuf(
1816:             (tw - box_w) / 2,
1817:             (th - box_h) / 2,
1818:             box_w,
1819:             box_h,
1820:         ))
1821:     } else {
1822:         // Fit: place the scaled content centered on a box-sized transparent canvas.
1823:         let canvas = Pixbuf::new(Colorspace::Rgb, true, 8, box_w, box_h)?;
1824:         canvas.fill(0);
1825:         scaled.composite(
1826:             &canvas,
1827:             x,
1828:             y,
1829:             tw,
1830:             th,
1831:             0.0,
1832:             0.0,
1833:             1.0,
1834:             1.0,
1835:             InterpType::Bilinear,
1836:             255,
1837:         );
1838:         Some(canvas)
1839:     }
1840: }

1842: /// Apply the directly-mappable style properties to any widget: visibility,
1843: /// opacity, size hints, content margins, plus CSS-backed decoration
1844: /// (background, border, font family/weight).
1845: fn apply_style(widget: &gtk::Widget, node: &HostNode) {
1846:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::VISIBLE) {
1847:         widget.set_visible(*bits != 0);
1848:     }
1849:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::OPACITY) {
1850:         widget.set_opacity(f64::from(f32::from_bits(*bits)));
1851:     }
1852:     // CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS → native overflow clipping (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity,
1853:     // spec LAYOUT.md / PRIMITIVES.md: a Fixed box constrains layout but only
1854:     // clips when this property is set).
1855:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS) {
1856:         widget.set_overflow(if *bits != 0 {
1857:             gtk::Overflow::Hidden
1858:         } else {
1859:             gtk::Overflow::Visible
1860:         });
1861:     }
1862:     let w = node.properties.get(&property_id::WIDTH).copied();
1863:     let h = node.properties.get(&property_id::HEIGHT).copied();
1864:     let sw = layout::size_hint(w);
1865:     let sh = layout::size_hint(h);
1866:     // FILL (-1.0) means "expand to available space": grow on the axis and align
1867:     // the widget into it (SwiftUI `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`). A finite
1868:     // value becomes a size request; HUG_CONTENT / absence leaves the natural size.
1869:     // A present-but-not-FILL axis resets a previous expansion so updates are
1870:     // idempotent; an absent axis is left untouched (preserves widget defaults
1871:     // such as Spacer's built-in expand).
1872:     if let layout::SizeHint::Fill = sw {
1873:         widget.set_hexpand(true);
1874:         widget.set_halign(Align::Fill);
1875:     } else if w.is_some() {
1876:         widget.set_hexpand(false);
1877:     }
1878:     if let layout::SizeHint::Fill = sh {
1879:         widget.set_vexpand(true);
1880:         widget.set_valign(Align::Fill);
1881:     } else if h.is_some() {
1882:         widget.set_vexpand(false);
1883:     }
1884:     if w.is_some() || h.is_some() {
1885:         widget.set_size_request(
1886:             match sw {
1887:                 layout::SizeHint::Fixed(v) => v,
1888:                 _ => -1,
1889:             },
1890:             match sh {
1891:                 layout::SizeHint::Fixed(v) => v,
1892:                 _ => -1,
1893:             },
1894:         );
1895:     }
1896:     // CONTENT_MARGINS is folded into the padding margins by `apply_padding` as
1897:     // the lowest-precedence base (per-edge PADDING_* > PADDING > CONTENT_MARGINS,
1898:     // spec PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model) — it must NOT be applied here,
1899:     // or it would override the higher-precedence PADDING margins.
1900: 
1901:     let css = style_css(node);
1902:     if !css.is_empty() {
1903:         widget.set_widget_name(&format!("pathland-{}", node.id));
1904:         let provider = gtk::CssProvider::new();
1905:         let _ = provider.load_from_data(&format!("#pathland-{} {{ {css} }}", node.id));
1906:         widget
1907:             .style_context()
1908:             .add_provider(&provider, gtk::STYLE_PROVIDER_PRIORITY_APPLICATION);
1909:     }
1910: }

1912: /// CSS decoration (background, border, font family) for a node, keyed by its
1913: /// widget name (set in [`apply_style`]).
1914: fn style_css(node: &HostNode) -> String {
1915:     let mut css = String::new();
1916:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR) {
1917:         let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(*bits);
1918:         css.push_str(&format!(
1919:             "background-color:rgba({:.0},{:.0},{:.0},{:.3});",
1920:             r * 255.0,
1921:             g * 255.0,
1922:             b * 255.0,
1923:             a
1924:         ));
1925:     }
1926:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_WIDTH) {
1927:         let w = f32::from_bits(*bits);
1928:         let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(node.u32_property(property_id::BORDER_COLOR, 0xFF00_0000));
1929:         css.push_str(&format!(
1930:             "border:{w}px solid rgba({:.0},{:.0},{:.0},{:.3});",
1931:             r * 255.0,
1932:             g * 255.0,
1933:             b * 255.0,
1934:             a
1935:         ));
1936:     }
1937:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_RADIUS) {
1938:         let r = f32::from_bits(*bits);
1939:         if r != 0.0 {
1940:             css.push_str(&format!("border-radius:{r}px;"));
1941:         }
1942:     }
1943:     if let Some(family) = node.string_property(property_id::FONT_FAMILY) {
1944:         css.push_str(&format!("font-family:'{}';", family.replace('\'', "\\'")));
1945:     }
1946:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::FONT_WEIGHT) {
1947:         let w = f32::from_bits(*bits);
1948:         if w > 0.0 {
1949:             css.push_str(&format!("font-weight:{w};"));
1950:         }
1951:     }
1952:     css
1953: }

1955: /// Apply color/font-size/font-weight text style from properties via Pango
1956: /// attributes.
1957: fn apply_text_style(label: &Label, node: &HostNode) {
1958:     let attrs = pango::AttrList::new();
1959:     if let Some(fs) = node.properties.get(&property_id::FONT_SIZE) {
1960:         let pts = (f32::from_bits(*fs).max(0.0) as i32) * 1000;
1961:         attrs.insert(pango::AttrSize::new(pts));
1962:     }
1963:     if let Some(color) = node.properties.get(&property_id::COLOR) {
1964:         let c = *color;
1965:         let red = (((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
1966:         let green = (((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
1967:         let blue = ((c & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
1968:         let mut fg = pango::AttrColor::new_foreground(red, green, blue);
1969:         fg.set_start_index(0);
1970:         fg.set_end_index(u32::MAX);
1971:         attrs.insert(fg);
1972:     }
1973:     label.set_attributes(Some(&attrs));
1974: 
1975:     // Layout (spec LAYOUT.md §content fitting): a Fixed `WIDTH` wraps the text
1976:     // within the box (a GTK label otherwise takes its natural un-wrapped width);
1977:     // `LINE_LIMIT` clamps the line count and truncates with an ellipsis, whose
1978:     // position follows `TRUNCATION_MODE` when present (Tail default). A
1979:     // `TRUNCATION_MODE` **alone** has no observable effect (SwiftUI-aligned):
1980:     // it never forces a single line and never truncates by itself.
1981:     let fixed_width = fixed_size(node, property_id::WIDTH).is_some();
1982:     let line_limit = node.properties.get(&property_id::LINE_LIMIT).copied();
1983:     let trunc = node
1984:         .properties
1985:         .get(&property_id::TRUNCATION_MODE)
1986:         .map(|b| f32::from_bits(*b) as u8);
1987:     if fixed_width || line_limit.is_some_and(|n| n > 0) {
1988:         label.set_wrap(true);
1989:         label.set_wrap_mode(pango::WrapMode::WordChar);
1990:     }
1991:     if let Some(n) = line_limit {
1992:         if n > 0 {
1993:             label.set_lines(n as i32);
1994:             // Only a LINE_LIMIT clamp truncates; TRUNCATION_MODE positions the
1995:             // ellipsis (renderer-owned fidelity: Start/Middle are reliable for
1996:             // single-line labels, best-effort on a multi-line clamp).
1997:             label.set_ellipsize(
1998:                 trunc
1999:                     .map(layout::ellipsize_from)
2000:                     .unwrap_or(pango::EllipsizeMode::End),
2001:             );
2002:         }
2003:     }
2004: }

2006: /// Run the GTK renderer over a shared ring, pumping frames in and waking the
2007: /// host on raw-input events.
2008: ///
2009: /// `on_event` is invoked (on the GTK main thread) with the shared ring whenever
2010: /// the renderer wrote a raw input; the app drains the ring's event queue itself
2011: /// (`RingTransport::drain_events`) and may re-emit a new frame.
2012: ///
2013: /// Passes the process's real program args to GTK (a native Rust binary's args
2014: /// are just its program name — safe for GTK to parse).
2015: pub fn run<F>(app_id: &str, title: &str, ring: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event: F)
2016: where
2017:     F: FnMut(Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>) + 'static,
2018: {
2019:     let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
2020:     let args: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
2021:     run_with_pump(app_id, title, ring, &args, on_event);

2042: /// [`run_with_pump`] with an explicit default window size (embedding hosts that
2043: /// know the UI needs more room, e.g. a master-detail layout, pass their own).
2044: pub fn run_with_pump_sized<P, F>(
2045:     app_id: &str,
2046:     title: &str,
2047:     pump: Rc<RefCell<P>>,
2048:     args: &[&str],
2049:     on_event: F,
2050:     default_width: i32,
2051:     default_height: i32,
2052: ) where
2053:     P: Pump + 'static,
2054:     F: FnMut(Rc<RefCell<P>>) + 'static,
2055: {
2056:     let app_id = app_id.to_string();
2057:     let title = title.to_string();
2058:     let on_event = Rc::new(RefCell::new(on_event));
2059: 
2060:     let app = gtk::Application::builder().application_id(&app_id).build();
2061: 
2062:     app.connect_activate(move |app| {
2063:         let window = gtk::ApplicationWindow::builder()
2064:             .application(app)
2065:             .title(&title)
2066:             .default_width(default_width)
2067:             .default_height(default_height)
2068:             .build();
2069: 
2070:         let renderer = Rc::new(RefCell::new(GtkRenderer::new()));
2071: 
2072:         // Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md): the renderer derives the
2073:         // effective scheme from the native GTK variant and re-resolves design
2074:         // tokens when it changes. Scheme is NEVER carried by the protocol.
2075:         if let Some(settings) = gtk::Settings::default() {
2076:             let renderer_for_scheme = renderer.clone();
2077:             settings.connect_gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme_notify(move |settings| {
2078:                 renderer_for_scheme
2079:                     .borrow_mut()
2080:                     .set_scheme(tokens::scheme_from_settings(settings));
2081:             });
2082:             renderer
2083:                 .borrow_mut()
2084:                 .set_scheme(tokens::scheme_from_settings(&settings));
2085:         }
2086: 
2087:         // Native inputs are written as EVENT opcodes into the pump (host → guest);
2088:         // the host is then woken to drain the event ring itself.
2089:         //
2090:         // `emit` is the shared path for every raw input the renderer reports —
2091:         // pointer/control events from the sink below, and platform back /
2092:         // Escape-key navigation from the window-level key controller.
2093:         //
2094:         // A frame apply borrows the pump zero-copy (the batch aliases the shared
2095:         // ring). Applying a value-bearing control's *programmatic* value
2096:         // (e.g. `GtkScale::set_value`) fires its connected GTK signal
2097:         // synchronously, re-entering `emit` while the pump is borrowed. Such
2098:         // events are deferred to the idle pump (flushed before the next frame),
2099:         // which also avoids a control echo loop when the host writes the same
2100:         // value back.
2101:         let pending: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Event>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
2102:         let emit = {
2103:             let pump = pump.clone();
2104:             let wake = on_event.clone();
2105:             let pending = pending.clone();
2106:             move |ev: Event| match pump.try_borrow_mut() {
2107:                 Ok(mut p) => {
2108:                     let _ = p.send_input(&ev);
2109:                     drop(p);
2110:                     wake.borrow_mut()(pump.clone());
2111:                 }
2112:                 Err(_) => {
2113:                     pending.borrow_mut().push(ev);
2114:                 }
2115:             }
2116:         };
2117:         {
2118:             let emit_for_sink = emit.clone();
2119:             let sink: Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut(Event)>> =
2120:                 Rc::new(RefCell::new(move |ev: Event| emit_for_sink(ev)));
2121:             renderer.borrow_mut().set_event_sink(sink);
2122: 
2123:             // Platform back: Escape (and BackSpace when no text entry has focus)
2124:             // is a native back request → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`. NAVIGATE
2125:             // is global (never node-keyed), so it is attached once at the window
2126:             // level, in the capture phase so it fires even when a child widget
2127:             // holds focus. BackSpace is only mapped when the focused widget is
2128:             // not a text input, so it never swallows text editing.
2129:             let emit_for_key = emit.clone();
2130:             let window_for_key = window.clone();
2131:             let key = EventControllerKey::new();
2132:             key.set_propagation_phase(PropagationPhase::Capture);
2133:             key.connect_key_pressed(move |_key, keyval, _code, _state| {
2134:                 let keyval = keyval.into_glib();
2135:                 let is_escape = keyval == gtk::gdk::ffi::GDK_KEY_Escape as u32;
2136:                 let is_backspace = keyval == gtk::gdk::ffi::GDK_KEY_BackSpace as u32
2137:                     && !window_has_text_focus(&window_for_key);
2138:                 if is_escape || is_backspace {
2139:                     emit_for_key(Event::Navigate { url: None });
2140:                     glib::Propagation::Stop
2141:                 } else {
2142:                     glib::Propagation::Proceed
2143:                 }
2144:             });
2145:             window.add_controller(key);
2146:         }
2147: 
2148:         // Initial render + window root. Deferred control signals from the mount
2149:         // apply are flushed before the idle pump takes over.
2150:         pump_once(&renderer, &pump);
2151:         flush_pending(&pump, &pending, &on_event);
2152:         let root = renderer.borrow().root_widget();
2153:         if let Some(root) = root {
2154:             window.set_child(Some(&root));
2155:         }
2156:         window.present();
2157: 
2158:         // Idle pump: flush any deferred (re-entrant) events, then apply pending
2159:         // frames to the renderer. Events are drained by the host (woken from the
2160:         // sink above), not here.
2161:         let idle_renderer = renderer.clone();
2162:         let idle_pump = pump.clone();
2163:         let idle_pending = pending.clone();
2164:         let idle_wake = on_event.clone();
2165:         glib::idle_add_local(move || {
2166:             flush_pending(&idle_pump, &idle_pending, &idle_wake);
2167:             pump_once(&idle_renderer, &idle_pump);
2168:             glib::ControlFlow::Continue
2169:         });
2170:     });
2171: 
2172:     // Run the GTK main loop with the caller-provided argv.
2173:     app.run_with_args(args);
2174: }

2176: /// Whether a text input currently holds keyboard focus, so backspace is not
2177: /// misread as a platform-back navigation while the user is editing text.
2178: fn window_has_text_focus(window: &impl IsA<gtk::Window>) -> bool {
2179:     let focused: Option<gtk::Widget> = window
2180:         .upcast_ref::<gtk::Window>()
2181:         .property::<Option<gtk::Widget>>("focus-widget");

2185: /// Flush events deferred during a frame apply (re-entrant control signals) into
2186: /// the pump and wake the host. Runs between frames, so the pump is free.
2187: fn flush_pending<P, F>(
2188:     pump: &Rc<RefCell<P>>,
2189:     pending: &Rc<RefCell<Vec<Event>>>,
2190:     wake: &Rc<RefCell<F>>,
2191: ) where
2192:     P: Pump,
2193:     F: FnMut(Rc<RefCell<P>>),
2194: {
2195:     if pending.borrow().is_empty() {
2196:         return;
2197:     }
2198:     let events = std::mem::take(&mut *pending.borrow_mut());
2199:     let mut p = pump.borrow_mut();
2200:     for ev in events {
2201:         let _ = p.send_input(&ev);
2202:     }
2203:     drop(p);
2204:     wake.borrow_mut()(pump.clone());
2205: }

2207: /// Apply pending frames to the renderer. (Events flow the other way: the
2208: /// renderer writes them; the host drains them — see [`Pump`].)
2209: fn pump_once<P>(renderer: &Rc<RefCell<GtkRenderer>>, pump: &Rc<RefCell<P>>)
2210: where
2211:     P: Pump,
2212: {
2213:     loop {
2214:         let mut pump_ref = pump.borrow_mut();
2215:         match pump_ref.next_frame() {
2216:             Ok(Some(batch)) => {
2217:                 let frame = batch.frame();
2218:                 renderer.borrow_mut().apply_frame(frame);
2219:             }
2220:             _ => break,
2221:         }
2222:     }
2223: }

141:     /// Re-resolve every `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed property against the theme, the
142:     /// active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain, materializing concrete
143:     /// values into [`HostNode::properties`] (numeric) or [`HostNode::strings`]
144:     /// (STRING tokens). The paths are kept in [`HostNode::token_refs`] for
145:     /// re-resolution on scheme change.
146:     pub fn resolve_tokens(&mut self) {
147:         let tables = TokenTables {
148:             overrides: &self.overrides,
149:             dark_overrides: &self.dark_overrides,
150:             defaults: &self.defaults,
151:             dark_defaults: &self.dark_defaults,
152:         };
153:         for node in self.nodes.values_mut() {
154:             let refs: Vec<(u16, String)> = node.token_refs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v.clone())).collect();
155:             for (prop, path) in refs {
156:                 if let Some(value) = resolve_token(&path, self.scheme, &tables) {
157:                     match value {
158:                         TokenValue::Str(s) => {
159:                             node.strings.insert(prop, s);
160:                         }
161:                         _ => {
162:                             if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
163:                                 node.properties.insert(prop, bits);
164:                             }
165:                         }
166:                     }
167:                 }
168:             }
169:         }

172:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
173:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
174:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
175:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
176:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
177:                     let id = op.a();
178:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
179:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
180:                     entry.id = id;
181:                     entry.component_type = ty;
182:                 }
183:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
184:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
185:                 }
186:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
187:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
188:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
189:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
190:                             p.children.push(child);
191:                         }
192:                     }
193:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
194:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
195:                     }
196:                 }
197:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
198:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
199:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
200:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
201:                     }
202:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
203:                         c.parent = None;
204:                     }
205:                 }
206:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
207:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
208:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
209:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
210:                             p.children.remove(pos);
211:                         }
212:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
213:                             p.children.len()
214:                         } else {
215:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
216:                         };
217:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
218:                     }
219:                 }
220:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => {
221:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
222:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
223:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
224:                         if vt == value_type::STRING {
225:                             // Resolve the arena offset into the actual text.
226:                             if let Ok(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
227:                                 n.strings.insert(prop_id, text.to_string());
228:                             }
229:                         } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
230:                             // A token reference: keep the path for resolution
231:                             // against the theme (spec/TOKENS.md). C is the arena
232:                             // offset of the token path.
233:                             if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
234:                                 n.token_refs.insert(prop_id, path.to_string());
235:                             }
236:                         } else {
237:                             n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
238:                         }
239:                     }
240:                 }
241:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
242:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
243:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
244:                     }
245:                 }
246:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
247:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
248:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
249:                     if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.a()) {
250:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
251:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
252:                             frame
253:                                 .arena_str(op.c())
254:                                 .map(|s| TokenValue::Str(s.to_string()))
255:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
256:                         } else {
257:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
258:                         };
259:                         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
260:                             self.dark_overrides.insert(bare.to_string(), value);
261:                         } else {
262:                             self.overrides.insert(path.to_string(), value);
263:                         }
264:                     }
265:                 }
266:                 _ => {}
267:             }
268:         }
269:         self.resolve_tokens();
270:     }

49: /// `None`.

101: /// Whether a node is **effectively `FILL`-sized on `axis`** — it is `FILL`
102: /// itself, a layout-greedy primitive that fills `axis` by nature, or (fill
103: /// propagation) a Hug-sized container whose subtree carries a `FILL`-sized
104: /// child / greedy filler on `axis`. A Fixed box bounds its subtree, so a
105: /// Fixed-sized container never propagates (its children fill within the box).
106: ///
107: /// `resolve` maps a child id to its node; pass a no-op resolver when the caller
108: /// has no tree (then only the node's own size kind / greediness is considered).
109: pub fn effective_fill(node: &HostNode, axis: Axis, main_axis: bool, tree: &RenderTree) -> bool {
110:     match axis_hint(node, axis) {
111:         SizeHint::Fill => return true,
112:         SizeHint::Fixed(_) => return false,
113:         SizeHint::None => {}
114:     }
115:     if greedy_fills(node, main_axis) {
116:         return true;
117:     }
118:     if !propagates_fill(node.component_type) {
119:         return false;
120:     }
121:     // A child's greedy nature is relative to its own parent (`node`): a child's
122:     // main axis is `axis` iff `node` is a stack whose main axis is `axis`.
123:     let child_main = stack_orientation(node.component_type)
124:         .map(|o| Axis::of(o) == axis)
125:         .unwrap_or(false);
126:     node.children
127:         .iter()
128:         .any(|&cid| tree.node(cid).is_some_and(|c| effective_fill(c, axis, child_main, tree)))
129: }

313: /// Compute a node's padding margins. Precedence (spec PRIMITIVES.md §stack
314: /// layout model): per-edge `PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT` > uniform `PADDING`
315: /// > `CONTENT_MARGINS` (the stack's content inset is the lowest-precedence base,
316: /// matching the HTML renderer where `PADDING` is emitted after `CONTENT_MARGINS`
317: /// and wins the cascade).
318: ///
319: /// Padding is **styling** (a DSL modifier), so it applies to any node, not just
320: /// stacks.
321: pub fn padding_from(node: &HostNode) -> Edges {
322:     let base = f32_prop(node, property_id::CONTENT_MARGINS)
323:         .map(round_nonneg)
324:         .unwrap_or(0);
325:     let uniform = f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING)
326:         .map(round_nonneg)
327:         .unwrap_or(base);
328:     Edges {
329:         top: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_TOP)
330:             .map(round_nonneg)
331:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
332:         right: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_RIGHT)
333:             .map(round_nonneg)
334:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
335:         bottom: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM)
336:             .map(round_nonneg)
337:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
338:         left: f32_prop(node, property_id::PADDING_LEFT)
339:             .map(round_nonneg)
340:             .unwrap_or(uniform),
341:     }
342: }

344: fn f32_prop(node: &HostNode, prop: u16) -> Option<f32> {
345:     node.properties.get(&prop).map(|bits| f32::from_bits(*bits))
346: }

348: fn round_nonneg(f: f32) -> i32 {
349:     f.max(0.0).round() as i32

352: /// The column count of a vertical grid (`GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`) from its
353: /// `GRID_COLUMNS` constructor property (the cell-axis count). `FILL` (-1.0), a
354: /// non-positive value, or absence means auto-fit.
355: pub fn grid_columns(node: &HostNode) -> Option<u32> {
356:     let w = f32_prop(node, property_id::GRID_COLUMNS)?;
357:     if w <= 0.0 {
358:         return None;
359:     }
360:     Some(w.round() as u32)
361: }
362: 
363: /// The row count of a grid from its `GRID_ROWS` constructor property — the
364: /// fixed track of a `LAZY_HGRID` (and a static `GRID`'s row count).
365: pub fn grid_rows(node: &HostNode) -> Option<u32> {
366:     let r = f32_prop(node, property_id::GRID_ROWS)?;
367:     if r <= 0.0 {
368:         return None;
369:     }
370:     Some(r.round() as u32)
371: }

373: /// Whether a grid is horizontal (`LAZY_HGRID`) — its fixed track is the rows
374: /// axis and cells flow column-major.
375: pub fn is_hgrid(component_type: u16) -> bool {
376:     component_type == component_type::LAZY_HGRID
377: }
378: 
379: /// A grid's fixed track count: `WIDTH`-style columns for vertical grids
380: /// (`GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`), `HEIGHT`-style rows for a horizontal `LAZY_HGRID`.
381: /// `None` (auto-fit) collapses to a single track.
382: pub fn grid_track(node: &HostNode) -> Option<u32> {
383:     if is_hgrid(node.component_type) {
384:         grid_rows(node)
385:     } else {
386:         grid_columns(node)
387:     }
388: }

390: /// Cell position for a grid child index. Vertical grids fill **row-major**
391: /// (`(row = index / track, col = index % track)`); a horizontal `LAZY_HGRID`
392: /// fills **column-major** (`(row = index % track, col = index / track)`).
393: pub fn grid_cell_position(index: u32, track: Option<u32>, horizontal: bool) -> (u32, u32) {
394:     let n = track.filter(|c| *c > 0).unwrap_or(1);
395:     if horizontal {
396:         (index % n, index / n)
397:     } else {
398:         (index / n, index % n)
399:     }
400: }
401: 
402: /// The grid's flattened `(cell, row, col)` placements (spec §GridRow): a
403: /// `GRID_ROW`'s children are one row's cells (always a new row starting at
404: /// column 0); bare cells auto-flow, advancing after `GRID_COLUMNS` — or the
405: /// widest row — columns. A short row leaves its trailing columns empty. A
406: /// horizontal `LAZY_HGRID` flattens `GRID_ROW` children too but places
407: /// column-major over `GRID_ROWS` tracks.
408: pub fn grid_cells(node: &HostNode, tree: &RenderTree) -> Vec<(u32, u32, u32)> {
409:     let horizontal = is_hgrid(node.component_type);
410:     let explicit = node
411:         .children
412:         .iter()
413:         .any(|&c| tree.node(c).is_some_and(|n| n.component_type == component_type::GRID_ROW));
414:     if !horizontal && explicit {
415:         // Widest-row columns when `GRID_COLUMNS` is absent (auto-fit).
416:         let track = grid_track(node).map(|t| t.max(1)).unwrap_or_else(|| {
417:             let mut width = 0u32;
418:             let mut run = 0u32;
419:             for &child in &node.children {
420:                 if tree.node(child).is_some_and(|n| n.component_type == component_type::GRID_ROW) {
421:                     width = width.max(tree.node(child).map(|n| n.children.len() as u32).unwrap_or(0));
422:                     run = 0;
423:                 } else {
424:                     run += 1;
425:                     width = width.max(run);
426:                 }
427:             }
428:             width.max(1)
429:         });
430:         let mut cells = Vec::new();
431:         let mut row = 0u32;
432:         let mut col = 0u32;
433:         for &child in &node.children {
434:             let Some(cn) = tree.node(child) else { continue };
435:             if cn.component_type == component_type::GRID_ROW {
436:                 if col > 0 {
437:                     row += 1;
438:                 }
439:                 col = 0;
440:                 for &cell in &cn.children {
441:                     cells.push((cell, row, col));
442:                     col += 1;
443:                 }
444:                 row += 1;
445:                 col = 0;
446:             } else {
447:                 if col >= track {
448:                     row += 1;
449:                     col = 0;
450:                 }
451:                 cells.push((child, row, col));
452:                 col += 1;
453:             }
454:         }
455:         return cells;
456:     }
457:     // Index-based placement (row-major, or column-major for an hgrid), with
458:     // `GRID_ROW` children flattened into their cells.
459:     let flat: Vec<u32> = node
460:         .children
461:         .iter()
462:         .flat_map(|&c| {
463:             if tree.node(c).is_some_and(|n| n.component_type == component_type::GRID_ROW) {
464:                 tree.node(c).map(|n| n.children.clone()).unwrap_or_default()
465:             } else {
466:                 vec![c]
467:             }
468:         })
469:         .collect();
470:     flat.into_iter()
471:         .enumerate()
472:         .map(|(i, c)| {
473:             let (row, col) = grid_cell_position(i as u32, grid_track(node), horizontal);
474:             (c, row, col)
475:         })
476:         .collect()
477: }

2: //!
3: //! The renderer owns default token values and the effective color scheme.
4: //! Tier-1 defaults start as **concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks**
5: //! ([`concrete_default_tables`]); when a real widget exists, the tokens the

8: //! `@borders`, `@success_color`, …). Headless / theme-missing → pure concrete

18: /// GTK theme named color → canonical Tier-1 token path. A resolver that returns

20: const NAMED_COLORS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[

34: /// Derive the effective scheme from a `GtkSettings` object.

36: pub fn scheme_from_settings(settings: &gtk::Settings) -> Scheme {
37:     let dark = settings.is_gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme()
38:         || settings
39:             .gtk_theme_name()
40:             .as_deref()
41:             .map_or(false, |name| name.ends_with("-dark"));
42:     if dark {
43:         Scheme::Dark
44:     } else {
45:         Scheme::Light
46:     }
47: }

49: /// Build the Tier-1 default tables (light + dark), replacing the tokens the
50: /// `resolve` closure can map (a widget's style-context theme lookup) with
51: /// native colors **for the given scheme**. GTK exposes one theme at a time, so
52: /// only the *active* scheme's defaults are native; the other scheme keeps its
53: /// concrete fallback.
54: pub fn enrich_defaults<F>(
55:     resolve: &F,
56:     scheme: Scheme,
57: ) -> (BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>, BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>)
58: where
59:     F: Fn(&str) -> Option<u32>,
60: {
61:     let (mut base, mut dark) = concrete_default_tables();
62:     let target = match scheme {
63:         Scheme::Dark => &mut dark,
64:         Scheme::Light => &mut base,
65:     };
66:     for (name, path) in NAMED_COLORS {
67:         if let Some(argb) = resolve(name) {
68:             target.insert((*path).to_string(), TokenValue::Color(argb));
69:         }
70:     }
71:     (base, dark)
72: }

74: /// Resolve a GTK theme named color (`@theme_*`, `@borders`, …) to
75: /// `0xAARRGGBB` via a style context, or `None` when the theme doesn't define it.
76: pub fn lookup_color(ctx: &gtk::StyleContext, name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
77:     ctx.lookup_color(name).map(|rgba| {
78:         let a = (rgba.alpha() * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u32;
79:         let r = (rgba.red() * 255.0).round() as u32;
80:         let g = (rgba.green() * 255.0).round() as u32;
81:         let b = (rgba.blue() * 255.0).round() as u32;
82:         (a << 24) | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b
83:     })
84: }

1: //! # Pathland GTK4 desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native GTK4 app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory ring**
4: //! and the shared **GTK renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter in
7: //! `pathland-core` emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and
8: //! the `pathland-render-gtk` renderer maps them onto native GTK widgets. The demo
9: //! never touches GTK/glib/pango directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::{listener, size};
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Align, Color, Node, View, ViewExt};
25: 
26: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.GtkDemo";
27: 
28: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
29: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
30: 
31: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter value. This is the developer's
32: /// authoring surface.
33: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>) -> Node {
34:     let tap_count = count.clone();
35:     vstack![
36:         hstack![
37:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str())
38:                 .frame(Some(size::FILL), None, None),
39:             button("Increment").on_tap_gesture(move || *tap_count.borrow_mut() += 1),
40:         ]
41:         .spacing(8.0)
42:         .padding(16.0),
43:         text("Pathland · GTK4 · shared ring").foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_888888)),
44:         // A non-button view (Text) declaring raw pointer listeners — proving any
45:         // element can emit events via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` property.
46:         text("I am a Text with raw pointer listeners")
47:             .pointer_events(listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP)
48:             .foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_0000AA)),
49:         vstack![
50:             text("short"),
51:             text("a much longer label"),
52:             text("x"),
53:         ]
54:         .spacing(4.0)
55:         .padding(16.0)
56:         .frame(None, None, Some(Align::Center)),
57:     ]
58:     .spacing(12.0)
59:     .padding(24.0)
60:     .build()
61: }
62: 
63: fn main() {
64:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new()));
65:     let ring = Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new()));
66:     let count = Rc::new(RefCell::new(0u32));
67:     let handlers = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TapHandlers::new()));
68: 
69:     // Build + emit the current tree, refreshing the id → tap-callback map.
70:     let emit = {
71:         let engine = engine.clone();
72:         let ring = ring.clone();
73:         let count = count.clone();
74:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
75:         move || {
76:             let mut tree = build_tree(&count);
77:             assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
78:             let mut h = handlers.borrow_mut();
79:             h.clear();
80:             pathland_view::collect_tap_handlers(&tree, &mut *h);
81:             drop(h);
82: 
83:             let mut ring_ref = ring.borrow_mut();
84:             let mut guest = ring_ref.producer();
85:             guest.begin_frame();
86:             engine.borrow_mut().emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
87:             guest.end_frame();
88:         }
89:     };
90: 
91:     // Initial frame before the renderer starts pumping.
92:     emit();
93: 
94:     // Hand the renderer the shared ring and a wake handler. The renderer writes
95:     // native inputs as EVENT opcodes into the ring and wakes us; we drain the
96:     // ring, run the taps through the recognizer, invoke the matching callback,
97:     // and re-emit. The renderer's idle pump applies the delta.
98:     pathland_gtk::run(APP_ID, "Pathland GTK4 Demo", ring.clone(), {
99:         let emit = emit;
100:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
101:         let start = Instant::now();
102:         let mut recognizer = pathland_view::TapRecognizer::new();
103:         move |ring| {
104:             let events = ring.borrow_mut().drain_events();
105:             let now_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
106:             let mut tapped = false;
107:             for ev in &events {
108:                 // Platform back (Escape/back key) arrives as a global NAVIGATE
109:                 // request with no URL. There is no Rust router yet, so this is
110:                 // surfaced to the console to prove the event reached the app.
111:                 if matches!(ev, pathland_core::Event::Navigate { url: None }) {
112:                     eprintln!("[demo] NAVIGATE back requested");
113:                 }
114:                 if let Some(target) = recognizer.feed(ev, now_ms) {
115:                     if let Some(handler) = handlers.borrow().get(&target) {
116:                         let mut cb = handler.borrow_mut();
117:                         (&mut *cb)();
118:                         tapped = true;
119:                     }
120:                 }
121:             }
122:             if tapped {
123:                 emit();
124:             }
125:         }
126:     });
127: }
